title: Billing Desk Note — Homeowner Charges on New Home Builder Warranties Claims
content:
On Bridgewell's New Home Builder Warranties the homeowner pays nothing for the warranty itself, but may be billed charges on a claim. This note states the billing rules for those homeowner charges.

## Rules

1. Each homeowner charge is billed once per claim and charge type.
2. Homeowner payments are applied to the open charges of the claim they name.

The charge types billed to a homeowner on a claim are the structural deductible, the systems extension deductible, the appliance service fee and the mediation fee. The homeowner's deductible balance is the total of the deductibles and fees billed to the homeowner on claims and not yet paid or waived: a charge raises it, and a homeowner payment or a credit lowers it. A homeowner charge is credited when a mediation fee is refunded after the homeowner prevails, or when a charge is waived or was billed in error.

## Rule 1 judged

Rule 1 is judged from the company's billing records before a charge is billed: the claim and the charge type together identify the charge.

| Already billed | Charge to be billed on a claim | Under rule 1 |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing on that claim | Mediation fee | Not barred |
| A mediation fee on that claim | Mediation fee | Not billed a second time |
| An appliance service fee on that claim | Mediation fee | Not barred: a different charge type |
| A mediation fee on another claim | Mediation fee | Not barred: a different claim |

## Rule 2 illustrated (hypothetical figures)

A homeowner has two claims with open charges: a 75.00 USD appliance service fee on the first claim and a 250.00 USD mediation fee on the second. A payment of 75.00 USD that names the first claim is applied to the first claim's open charge, leaving the second claim's mediation fee open; the deductible balance falls from 325.00 USD to 250.00 USD.
